endorsements.quote: This also bounds agentic AI: an agent may orchestrate authoring, gather metadata, or propose changes, but must not mutate approved artifacts or start production execution without crossing the same boundary as human-authored changes.
Custom logic should be promoted to a capability and governed through the capability lifecycle.

Construction-time traceability explains how a workflow came into existence: approved specification, registry snapshot, composer version, validation report, resolved capability versions, canonical definition, and hash.

unlisted_practices: Separate AI-assisted authoring from execution so that AI-drafted artifacts remain non-executable until validated, reviewed, approved, and version-published.
Express transformation intent in a machine-readable specification that references only approved, versioned capabilities in a governed registry.
Use a deterministic composer to validate specifications against a pinned registry snapshot and emit a construction trace before any workflow is executed.
Require pinning of capability versions for approved production execution while allowing controlled migration.
Block deprecated capabilities for new compositions unless a recorded exception is made.
Do not use AI model self-explanations or reasoning traces as the basis of regulated execution; confine execution by specifications, tests, contracts, approvals, and traces.
Do not allow AI to approve its own tests as sufficient evidence.
Treat data preparation such as date formatting and unit conversion as approved, governed capabilities rather than embedded scripts.
Provide AI code generation with behavioral specifications plus project conventions, tests, type context, and helper signatures to ensure correct and integrable output.
Keep contract quality under human review at approval, since the composer does not certify contract correctness.

screen.reason: This is a framework paper and industrial experience report proposing specification-driven composition as a design/governance framework for using AI in regulated clinical data transformation workflows.
